summary: The Legacy IT Reduction Act of 2026 requires each federal agency’s Chief Information Officer to compile and update an inventory of legacy IT systems within one year and every five years thereafter, and to develop and submit a modernization plan every five years that prioritizes updates, retirements, or disposals, with OMB issuing implementation guidance and the Comptroller General reviewing progress after three years.

scores.thoughts: The bill's explicit purpose is to reduce federal reliance on and expenditures for legacy IT systems through mandatory inventories and modernization plans. Section 8 prohibits new appropriations, and the focus on retiring outdated systems implies long-term spending reductions via efficiency gains. This directly engages the topic of government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, or revenue collection.
The bill addresses only internal federal IT systems and modernization planning; it has no connection to healthcare policy or delivery models.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The legislation is limited to federal IT inventory and planning; it does not touch immigration policy or enforcement.
No references to reproductive health, abortion access, or related regulations appear in the text.
National security systems are explicitly exempted (section 7(b)), and the bill does not alter defense budgets or IT spending within the Department of Defense.
The bill makes no mention of environmental regulations, climate policy, or related standards.
No provisions affect welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net funding.
The bill is confined to federal agency IT systems and does not address education funding, schools, or choice programs.
No content relates to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
The legislation does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
While the bill promotes IT cost reduction, it does not set fiscal targets, address deficits, or prioritize debt reduction as policy.
The bill contains no language concerning civil rights, nondiscrimination, or LGBTQ+ protections.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid programs.
The legislation does not touch election administration, voting access, or election integrity measures.
Although the bill concerns federal IT systems, it focuses solely on legacy-system inventories and modernization plans; it does not regulate data privacy, tech oversight, or private-sector technology.
No provisions affect labor rights, union power, or employer flexibility.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or related conflicts.
